newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 18.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 18. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said it was not true he had "bargained" with the United States over the World Trade Organisation's Information Technology Agreement and Jakarta's controversial national car policy.
Police in West Java shot and killed four suspected criminals who tried to run away during an operation in which a number of known criminals were rounded-up in a sweep.
Officials at the central bank want the government to draft rules to stop money laundering as there were no clear-cut guidelines to stop the practice in Indonesia.
President Suharto has told regional officials to use their initiative in implementing development programmes and not rely on the central government.
Mobile telephone operator PT Satelindo said it needs 1.5 billion rupiah to expand its mobile telephone network to all of Indonesia's provinces.
President Suharto on Tuesday officiated the roll-out of the first locally made railway locomotive which will be exported to the Philippines.
